title: Going AWOL on the post after the band broke up
summary: Strained by night duty, he simply started walking off to the movies and cafeteria each day, slipping back to sleep, for two weeks, until he decided to report himself.

story.theme_name: Drafted: musicians in the military and the war years
story.community_name: Drafted: service bands, USO shows and the war years

blocks.x: So anyway, while we were there they broke it up, so I said now I'm going to have to do something. So this particular day I just got up -- they were doing different things. They were coming around and giving you different duties and so on.

One time I was in charge of quarters. I had to wake the soldiers up at 4:00 o'clock in the morning, and you stay up all night then you sleep all day. I was going through tremendous strain. So I just casually started walking one morning. I walked, must have been two miles. I just walked these two miles, thinking. So I said, well, I know what I'll do now. So I went to the movies and I went in a little cafeteria there and got something to eat and sat around. Then I went back to camp. Then I realized that I was AWOL. I said, that's good, but I didn't leave the camp. I was AWOL on the camp. So I kept that up for about a week. I kept it up for two weeks. I'd slip back in the barracks at night and go to sleep and get up early in the morning and leave again. So this one day the fellow came to me, one of the sergeants. He said, "The police are looking for you." You know, the military police. He said -- I said, "Well, that's simple. You just didn't see me. That's all." He said, "Well, they --," I said, "Well, don't worry about it. You just haven't seen me. Simple." So then finally, I kept it up, so then I realized that you know, you can't keep this up. You've got to do something. So I saw one of the Lieutenants, who was a recorder in the -- you know, they interview each soldier. You know, they was turning the whole thing around. So to cut it down, anyway, I said, "Well, do you think I should go to see these people who are looking for me?" He said, "Well, you know, what do you think? Do you

think you should?" I said, "Yes, I think I should now, because I would have to do something eventually. I can't keep this up." And I knew that if I'd run away, left the post and went home, you know, that would be worse. So I decided to go in front of the Board, you know. So I went to the barrack. I got all cleaned up, you know, and shaved. I guess I looked like an I don't know what, you know.
